In response to the recent market volatility across $TSM to $SKHY to Innolight:

- Taiwan to restrict borrowed share short selling from 30% -> 3% relative to order volumes (90% reduction),  effective Nov 9th. 

Taiwan is separately raising its minimum collateral requirement from 90% to 130% for margin short selling.

And authorized the $15.3B stabilization fund for Government buying in the stock market. 

- South Korea to waive 140% margin-loan collateral maintenance for 3 months to reduce forced selling, effective Nov 9th. 

- China introduced a series of stock-market support package aimed at stabilizing equities. People's Bank of China introduced a $15 billion liquidity-swap operation for securities firms and fund managers.

As well as reduced lending rates for the share buybacks and shareholder purchase programs from 1.25% -> 1% this month. 

_

Not saying what direction stocks would go, but with Countries heavily tied to the AI trade introducing short selling restrictions, share repurchases, and reduced margin collateral. 

These market mechanics are bullish for near term market stability + potential reversal in equities.

Everyone’s a long term investor for 2027, 2028, or 2029 onward

Until their portfolio experiences volatility months in. I still think:

- $RKLB could end up the next $SPCX

- $NBIS has the potential to be the next hyperscaler

- $SIVE has moonshot potential to be the next $LITE

- 1-3x P/E memory companies and $AXTI substrate bottlenecks are more durable than markets think

And that it’s stupid to sell single digit fwd P/E AI companies or promising longs.

And rotate that into 5% growth towel resellers at 47x P/E. Or 180x cyber companies, just because they’re going up.

I’ve seen $AMD go from the $3 valley of doom to $400 as people thought it could be the next $INTC / $NVDA.

And been through the Bitcoin $1000 -> $18,000 -> $3000 -> $100,000 cycle.

Not advice on how to position or trade, but anyone on extreme leverage during those times got wiped out. 

While the underlying assets sharply recovered later.

I do think AI, Space, and Physical AI are the future.

So, I’m remaining long, and using this time to maximize exposure to the winners

@Jsjsjsjd88 $IREN 90% GPU capex prepayment on a 5Y contract is exceptionally bullish and surprising to say the least...

Especially given market concerns over Neocloud financing.

$AAOI earnings:

- $1B-$1.5B LTA disclosed with a hyperscaler customer

- 2nd LTA coming soon, worth 5x+ more (implying $5B-$7.5B), in its final stages. 

This LTA explicitly includes lasers, very material for AOI that they're moving to supplying merchant lasers. 

- "The demand is exceptional, unprecedented. I do not know what kind of superlatives to use to describe the amount of demand that we are seeing out there in the industry"

Yeah this commentary doesn't sound like any optical demand would slowed down if it's "exceptional + unprecedented" 

- Rejected hyperscaler slowdowns from political changes with little effect. 

- AOI Can only meet 80% of demand, in case there's a kind of reduction, the demand would be bigger than AOI future capacity

- Moving toward other financing methods than ATMs (thank god), US bank loans similar to what $NBIS is doing, I'd argue is positive, given FCF coming in later. 

- Delay in meeting capacity projections into H1 2027. $471m/month targets pushed back into H2 2027, due to electrical procurement and construction logistics, which existed before Texas governor changed. 

This part is negative part of the earnings call. To qualify this, I don't quite think hyperscalers would sign a $5-$7.5B LTA if they didn't think AOI couldn't deliver.

-  Near term Q4 guidance cut was DSP availability. AOI revised near term projections down slightly to $385M and $420M in revenue. 

Said DSP supply would ease early 2027 and that they're qualifying more suppliers. 

- Gave hiked H2 2027 capacity projections from their expansion, near term revision downward. 

- 4 to 5 ongoing UHP laser eval/quals for CPO

UHP laser segment alone would far outweigh their $3.8B MC, especially if you're executing on multi billion dollar contracts with 60%+ gross margin laseres.

TLDR:
- Long term visibility improved a lot, with est. $6-$9B cumulative LTA contracts coming soon. 
- Shift toward supplying CPO lasers merchant is fundamentally material vs. just transceivers, and what I wanted to hear
- Capacity guidance hiked into H2 2027, near term delays from electrical/DSP related procurement + installation.  

I still think we're reached peak fear levels, but wouldn't dismiss disappointing short term procurement delays + Q4 DSP bottlenecks. 

AOI likely signing an additional +$5-$7.5B in likely hyperscaler LTAs and entering merchant UHP CPO market dominanted by $LITE + $COHR. 

Factored in with the valuation drop has made medium-long term opportunities very compelling.

@andrewdfeldman @CulperResearch @cerebras Glad to see a direct response from $CBRS about the short report

Elon is the perfect example though, on what you should do to dispute the BS

If there’s a false WSJ report or X post on $TSLA or $SPCX… Even if it’s something as little as space datacenters won’t work, he just calls it out real time.

I’m not saying every industry executive should do this, but at least hire a representative to defend against misleading narratives

I’m just calling out what I see with a failure in corporate communication, when so much is at stake.

I’m really not sure why SK Hynix/Samsung representing SK’s economy let narratives of memory oversupply be dominated by their own customers on X.

Or why $CBRS, which lost billions in valuation after the short seller report, is waiting for an analyst question in earnings to fix the damage 

Or why many of the “guppies” that would face a death in the Neocloud market aren’t actively fighting back against that claim here.

A lot of narratives and claims originated and were distributed via X.

Even if you don’t like Elon or X, even the Democratic Party combats narratives here as seen with the ratio on the VP’s New York post

I don’t see why this can’t be done with AI companies calling BS on $4 B300 price gluts.

That’s just blatantly false, there’s heavy industry doubts if MicroLED are even commercializable for CPO.

Also regarding $COHR on optical demand: “We continue to see no signs of attenuation in demand.”

Laser demand is independently as strong as memory, and Coherent / Lumentum wouldn’t be signing $20B or $5B LTAs left and right.

Yes $AAOI had a massive InP substrate purchase order earlier, and I don’t believe all of that is going toward transceiver lasers that Rosenblatt modeled.

I believe have the similar 60%+ GM UHP laser capabilities that $COHR $20B LTAs and $LITE $5B LTAs are primarily for.

While having a MC of <$5B and we’ll see some announcements there later.

As for $SIVE, it’s mainly about qualifications given they have the capacity now with foundries + 100m laser expansion plan. 

$MRVL + $LITE gives it an extremely clear window of opportunity as well, alongside current laser bottlenecks for qualifying players like $CRDO, Innolight, Cambridge, and hyperscalers.

We’ll see what new partners they announce in earnings this month.

Given both their tiny $600m, ~$4.9B MCs, I would not be surprised if their 2028 revenue exceeded their valuations.

$COHR earnings transcript TLDR:

Q: On $LITE + $MRVL merger.

A. Customers will prefer an independent optical supplier without competitive conflicts (opportunity for other merchant laser suppliers)

Q: Loop Capital asked about 2028 laser industry oversupply.

A: No oversupply risk by 2028. Coherent’s entire current internal InP production is consumed by its own products while its expanding capacity.

Q: On Chinese laser competition for CPO UHP lasers

A: “We really only have one competitor” (hinting at $LITE). 

Q: On financing concerns for capacity expansion during this market scare

A: Customer LTAs have prepayments, which are used for product capacity orders

2027 completely sold out, LTAs extend to 2030, customers placing orders into 2028.

Q: On laser technology for CPO scale up from Bernstein, whether it’s VCSELs or CW lasers.

A: CW for CPO scale out and scale up for 2026-2027.

2029-2030 sees scale in and chip to chip using micro-VCSELs, and 2028 opportunities for NPO scale up.

So technology of choice is CW for CPO.

- Coherent is seeing pricing power and raising margin targets, supporting view optical players get additional leverage for margin expansion

- Massive new $20B 5Y LTA, anchored by UHP CW lasers, with other optical products mixed in

- demand comes from growth in DC and conversion of copper interconnects to optics. The latter is bandwidth requirements, independent of DC growth.

slower compute growth can coexist with sharply rising optical content per system

TLDR:

- nothing quite showing optical demand like $20B in LTAs anchored by high power lasers from 1 customer alone (not your frontier labs type commitments)

- no industry wide laser oversupply risk by 2028 for InP lasers/EML 

- financing funded by revenue from LTAs and purchase orders.

- doesn’t see Chinese competition for high end lasers, commentary casts doubts over China capability + capacity expansion claims

- CW lasers weapon of choice for CPO, blended margins going up for optical players

- optics more isolated in the event of a DC slowdown 

Quite wild to see fundamentals of optical players improve so much, while overall valuations crash.

Reminds me of the time the former $TSM chairman bought $7.8M of $MU back in the $300's. https://t.co/KLXXwqtL9f

Cyberoffense/defense is probably going to eat up a TON of compute and end up a continuous compute-intensive arms race. 

Even $AMZN CEO thinks cybersecurity would take up 20% of tokens consumed for the next year. 

It's literally a problem of how much you throw at compute for vulnerability discovery + model capability, from of my chats w/ Horizon3. 

And this is going to become a nation state issue, as seen with the implications already with PHP to vulnerabilities with banks/infrastructure from AI swarms. 

But people see this and throw money at $CRWD, $NET, and others, which I was saying was a bubble. 

If it's a compute issue, the economics go to the infra, from neoclouds to $NBIS to networking like $AAOI. 

We'll likely see swarms go wild from aggressor nation states in the next few years. 

And any country, whether that's Japan or EU that don't have their own capabilities might suffer severe damage. 

US spent $11T+ cumulatively (inflation adjusted) on Nuclear weapons and we're like ~$1.8T into the the "cyber-nuclear weapon" equivalent of that

And this is not even including the endless other economic implications from AI in other fields from advancing cancer discovery to workforce automation with physical AI. 

It's hard to measure AI sustainability if $50K in compute spend from a foreign actor can take down $10B of your own infrastructure. 

AI has become a bipartisan national security issue, and even Democrats would not want China overtake the US in this field.

With $AXTI, even if demand was cut 50%, they'd still likely be sold out.

Since customers are asking for 3x+ their contracted volumes. I'd argue InP substrates are just as severe as lasers. 

In just 90 days, $AXTI literally went from:

Q2 backlog: $100m 
Q3 backlog: $500m+

With an extra $300-$400m+ from ordinary business, not multi-year agreements from $LITE / $COHR. 

I'm sure there's some double ordering but the materials are just so cheap relative to overall BOM, that it's spare change.

For companies like $SIVE / $AAOI, the demand imbalance for lasers are so severe

That even a 20-30% overall demand reduction from a hypothetical DC slowdown would likely not eliminate the shortage. 

We're seeing this before the next architectural shifts, where $NVDA Jensen Huang expects 15x optical volume for CPO scale-up. 

And as more hyperscalers commit to NPO as seen with $LITE new $5B UHP laser contracts. 

I'd argue this is more nuanced since I can't say the same for finished 800G/1.6T pluggables or lower end 70mW-100mW laser ranges that are currently bottlenecks. 

But this argument is more toward higher spec lasers. 

$AAOI is vertically integrated and has 300-400 mW capabilities, so they have the capability to shift attention to merchant lasers over supplying end-to-end optical transceivers. 

$SIVE is more pure play on this laser bottleneck, but they have the capabilities for 200mW + higher margin multiwavelength NPO/CPO lasers. 

I'd argue this is specifically the case for bottlenecks where demand imbalances are so deep (creating higher long term visibility, such as HBM). 

Whether it's large body substrates from $ATS that's bottlenecking Marvell + $AMD or lasers from $LITE that are sold out into 2029. 

or liquid transformers that have 4-5 year lead times. 

They they would still sell out of capacity even if overall demand decreased. 

If markets de-risked, it would make sense to hit optical module manufacturing players, maybe server rack assembly, to companies that still require heavy financing like Neoclouds.

And obviously haircut growth valuations (but not to the point where demand collapses to 0).

Yet we're seeing everything in AI trade is getting lumped up together as something that requires heavy financing + not profitable.

If a company is valued at $2B, has ~$1B in cash/inventory... And makes $354M FCF a quarter. 

Then returns 30-50% of FCF for dividends next year. 

I'd argue it's more of a matter of time before shareholder returns/fundamentals, (especially memory) overpower forced selling. 

But stock prices can look really dislocated from actual performance for periods of time, like now. 

Same with photonics, but that's more of a 2027-2028 growth type story with CPO + more optical content/xpu.

Laser companies like $LITE, $AAOI, and potentially $SIVE depending on quals, would likely be printing few years after capacity expansion comes online.

And it's already been largely funded... Lumentum with $NVDA + hyperscalers, AOI with $1.6B+ in ATMs, Sivers with 700M SEK from institutions. 

Compared to other sectors that still require a lot of capital for their buildouts.

Lot of funds / pods reportedly blew up recently so there's been a lot of forced selling. 

For example... even if $POET goes below their net cash (we're getting close), funds can be forced to liquidate holdings anyway. 

Even if another name looks operationally bullish like $NBIS, stock prices can look catastrophic and irrational until deleveraging stops.

Little rant, but to show you how rampant deleveraging has become:

- $CIFR is worth 44% LESS than when they announced their initial $GOOGL / $AMZN colo deals. 

- $AAOI is now ~ the same price BEFORE they secured major hyperscaler orders, raised $1.6B for capacity expansion and gave their suprising initial -> $378M+ projection ->  ~$471M revenue forecast.

- $ESMT ($2B MC) is the perfect example representing the memory sector.

B-BUT AI NAMES ARE NOT PROFITABLE??? Q3 Earnings: $526.2M gross profit, $330M net income.

To give you a comparison of what that looks like, the net income of $CRWD ($251B MC) was literally $5.3M. 

$NOW ($113B MC) was $277M.
$TSLA ($1.5T) was $787M.

Different industries/durability, but if we care about what's actually hitting the balance sheet: 

ESMT is sitting on ~$937M in net assets ($740M net cash, $278M inventory, etc), so EV goes down to $1.2B ish.

Annualized P/E: 1.6x...

People keep saying "Peak Earnings", "Cyclical", "no moat" but who in the world would want to build an old ass DDR2 line + fab and qualify it?

From ESMT commentary, we'll likely see ASP hikes Q4 to make up for potential consumer demand dropping. 

And further supply tightening with Samsung/Micron discontinuing DDR2/DDR3 lines.

Winbond was leaving DDR2 lines to pursue higher end memory. People keep saying China, but even Gigadevice was leaving DDR3 to pursue higher end memory. "DDR3's share of our DRAM revenue will continue to decline until we eventually stop selling DDR3 products."Nanya discontinued DDR2 lines few days ago. 

This is while majority of ESMT revenue comes from DDR2/DDR3. In ~3 quarters of constant earnings, ESMT would have more assets than their entire MC.

Who is going to stop buying $40 DLink cameras if their $3 memory cost goes to $3.5?

$MU / Samsung / $SKHY / $SNDK share similar parallels where durability is contractually enforced via take/pay LTAs with price floors.

But markets are pretending that it just won't happen, despite Samsung already being the most profitable company in the world. 

Markets should care about how much FCF is actually hitting the balance sheets, but are just indiscriminately selling off everything now.

But continue rotating capital into 47x P/E companies like Walmart or 180x forward P/E names like $CRWD.

We’re seeing the great rotation into safe, quality assets.

The rhetoric on X and from Elon leans overwhelmingly apocalyptic on Democrats winning.

It's a mini bubble here, but I think people forget AI is bipartisan national security priority, and that $NVDA's historic rally + AI buildout acceleration happened under the Biden admin.

Anyone can extrapolate a politician's negative view on AI to doompost indexes or that " $CRWV is going to go down".

But in all reality, even with a Democratic governor, we'll likely just see some headwinds to individual developers, and incentives like "clean-energy tax credits" moving to other areas in AI like solar manufacturing. 

Rather than any market-wide doomsday scenario that the opposing party likes to portray. 

Even Bitcoin/Ethereum performed better under the negatively perceived regulation of Gary Gensler. 

Just like any major event, everyone looks at the worst case scenario like helium disruption shutting down Samsung, $TSM, and the memory trade... 

Then markets move on few weeks later.
